title: Student identity linked to submission data
description: The student's identity (via login credentials and student ID) can be linked to their assignment submission data (work file, course, timestamp), creating a persistent association between the student and their academic work.
assumptions: The system stores and processes both identity and submission data in a way that allows correlation.

title: Assignment submission data disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: The Grades Portal Web App may expose student submission data (work file, student ID, course, timestamp) to unauthorized users or systems, violating confidentiality requirements.
assumptions: The system has inadequate access controls or data protection measures for submission data.

title: Unauthorized submission usurpation
description: An attacker could potentially submit assignments on behalf of a student by exploiting authentication weaknesses, leading to false attribution of academic work.
assumptions: The authentication mechanism has vulnerabilities or the system lacks proper verification of student identity during submission.

title: Transmission of Student Identifiers to Grading Service
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) transmits student id, course, file reference, and requesting role to the Assignment & Grading Service (P2). This creates an identifier threat as the data contains unique references to student identity that are being shared across system boundaries.
assumptions: Student identifiers are transmitted in clear or insufficiently protected form during the P1→P2 flow.
uncertainty_note: Citation I.2.1.1 from context applies to identifier threats generally; confidence in exact node match is moderate.

title: Processing of Identified Student Data
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) receives and processes identified data including student id, course, and file reference. This constitutes processing of identified data as defined in threat tree node I.1.1.
assumptions: P2 processes the received data for grading and assignment management purposes.
uncertainty_note: Citation I.1.1 from context applies to processing of identified data; confidence in exact node match is moderate.

title: Non-repudiation of Submission and Grading Actions
description: The flow transmits requesting role and file reference for submissions and grading requests. This creates non-repudiation concerns where individuals may be unable to deny their involvement in the system, as the data collected provides evidence of their actions.
assumptions: The system logs and processes submission/grading requests with role attribution.
uncertainty_note: Context [4] describes non-repudiation as a threat type; exact tree node Nr.1.1 is inferred based on standard LINDDUN Pro structure.

title: Unintended Data Disclosure via Assignment Storage
description: The Assignment & Grading Service stores student id, course, and submission time in the Assignment Store. While this is the intended purpose, there is a risk that this data could be disclosed beyond the necessary scope (e.g., to unauthorized parties, or in a format that enables re-identification). The minimality principle requires that only strictly required personal data be stored.
assumptions: The system may not have proper access controls or data minimization policies in place.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 based on context [5] which describes data disclosure as transfer across boundaries; this is an implicit disclosure risk.

title: Linkability of Student Assignment Data
description: Student id stored in the Assignment Store could be linked to other student records or data sources, potentially enabling correlation of assignment submissions with other personal information about the student.
assumptions: Other student data systems exist that could be cross-referenced with this assignment data.
uncertainty_note: Linkability threat based on student id being a unique identifier that could be correlated with other datasets.

title: Identifiability of Student through Assignment Data
description: The combination of student id, course, and submission time makes the data directly identifiable. Even if student id were anonymized, the course and submission time combination could potentially identify the student in certain contexts.
assumptions: Student id is a unique identifier that directly links to the student's identity.
uncertainty_note: Identifiability is inherent in storing student id; this is a fundamental characteristic of the data flow.

title: Teacher account impersonation during login
description: An attacker could impersonate a teacher during the login process, gaining unauthorized access to the Grades Portal Web App and viewing student submissions they should not have access to.
assumptions: Authentication mechanism is not sufficiently secure; attacker has access to teacher credentials or can bypass authentication.
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is inferred based on standard usurpation threat patterns; exact node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student submission data
description: The Grades Portal Web App may disclose student submission data to unauthorized parties, either through insecure data transmission, improper access controls, or data leakage during processing.
assumptions: Data is transmitted or stored without adequate encryption or access controls; system has vulnerabilities that could expose student data.
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is inferred based on standard disclosure threat patterns; exact node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Teacher identity linked to submission review activity
description: The system may process and store data that links a teacher's identity to their review activity and the specific submissions they access, potentially enabling profiling or tracking of teacher behavior.
assumptions: System logs or stores metadata about which teacher accessed which submissions; this data is retained and potentially accessible.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 from context §I.1.1 Processing of identified data applies to this scenario where teacher identity is processed with submission data.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student submission data
description: Student personal information (names, work content, submission times) displayed to teacher could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through compromised portal access or teacher misuse
uncertainty_note: Using standard LINDDUN Pro threat-tree node D.1.1 for disclosure threats; context [3][4] confirms Process→ExternalEntity supports all threat types at S/fl/D positions

title: Unauthorized access to student submission data
description: Student submission data could be accessed by unauthorized individuals through compromised portal credentials or insufficient access controls
uncertainty_note: Using standard LINDDUN Pro threat-tree node U.1.1 for usurpation threats; context [3][4] confirms Process→ExternalEntity supports all threat types at S/fl/D positions

title: Potential violation of student privacy regulations
description: Sharing student personal information with teachers must comply with FERPA/GDPR requirements; improper data handling could result in regulatory non-compliance
uncertainty_note: Using standard LINDDUN Pro threat-tree node Nc.1.1 for non-compliance threats; context [3][4] confirms Process→ExternalEntity supports all threat types at S/fl/D positions

title: Linkability of student data across systems
description: Teacher could potentially link student submission data with other student information they have access to, creating a comprehensive profile
uncertainty_note: Using standard LINDDUN Pro threat-tree node L.1.1 for linkability threats; context [3][4] confirms Process→ExternalEntity supports all threat types at S/fl/D positions

title: Student and Grader Identification from Grade Records
description: Grade records contain student id and grader id, enabling direct identification of students and graders. This creates privacy risks for both parties.
assumptions: Student and grader IDs are stored in the grade record

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: Grade records stored in DS2 contain sensitive academic information (grades, feedback) that could be accessed by unauthorized parties if database security is inadequate.
assumptions: Database access controls may not be sufficient
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard database security practices may not be fully implemented

title: Excessive Data Collection via Feedback Field
description: The feedback field may collect more personal information than necessary for grading purposes, potentially including subjective comments that reveal grader opinions or student performance details beyond the grade itself.
assumptions: Feedback field may contain detailed comments
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual feedback content and purpose

title: Grader Identity Usurpation
description: Grader id in the grade record could be impersonated if authentication mechanisms are weak, allowing unauthorized individuals to appear as legitimate graders.
assumptions: Authentication controls may be insufficient
uncertainty_note: Likelihood depends on authentication system strength

title: Linkability of Grade Records to Other Data
description: Grade records with student id, course, and timestamp could be linked to other student records, course enrollment data, or institutional databases, creating comprehensive profiles.
assumptions: Other institutional data systems exist that could be linked
uncertainty_note: Depends on institutional data architecture

title: Processing of identified student grade data
description: The system processes the student's grades and feedback, which are identified personal data. This processing could expose the student's academic performance to unauthorized parties or create privacy risks through data handling.
assumptions: Grades and feedback are considered identified personal data that can be linked to the student's identity.
uncertainty_note: Citation [5] from context supports I.1.1 node for processing identified data.

title: Linkability of student grades to identity
description: Student grades could be linked to their identity through the grades portal, potentially enabling tracking of academic performance across time or correlating with other data sources.
assumptions: Grades are inherently linked to student identity through the portal access mechanism.
uncertainty_note: Standard LINDDUN L threat for data flows involving personal information.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student grades
description: Student grades and feedback could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through vulnerabilities in the web application, improper access controls, or data leakage.
assumptions: The web application may have security vulnerabilities or insufficient access controls.
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 is a standard disclosure threat node for data flows.

title: Parent Account Impersonation During Login
description: An attacker could impersonate a parent during the login process, gaining unauthorized access to view their child's grades through the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Weak authentication mechanisms or credential theft

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child's Grades
description: Child's grade information could be disclosed to unauthorized parties (other parents, unauthorized users) through the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls or data exposure vulnerabilities

title: Child Identifiability Through Grade Data
description: Grade data could be used to identify the specific child, potentially revealing sensitive personal information about the student.
assumptions: Grade data contains or can be combined with identifying information

title: Excessive Data Collection for Grade Access
description: The system may collect more personal data than necessary to simply display grades, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: System collects unnecessary PII during parent authentication or grade retrieval

title: Unauthorized Access to Child's Grades Data
description: The grades portal web app (P1) transmits sensitive child academic information to the parent (EE2). If authentication or authorization controls are inadequate, unauthorized parties could intercept or access this data during transmission or storage.
assumptions: The system relies on proper authentication and encryption mechanisms to protect data in transit and at rest.
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as a representative disclosure threat node for Process->ExternalEntity flows.

title: Child Identifiability from Grades Data
description: The grades, feedback, and submission history displayed to the parent could potentially identify the child, especially if combined with other information. Even with the parent as the intended recipient, there's a risk of data being used to identify the child to third parties.
assumptions: The data contains unique identifiers or patterns that could link to the specific child.
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 as a representative identifiability threat node.

title: Parent Identity Usurpation
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate the parent (EE2) to access the child's grades data through the portal (P1). This could occur through credential theft, session hijacking, or social engineering attacks.
assumptions: The authentication mechanism for parent access is vulnerable to credential compromise or session attacks.
uncertainty_note: Using U.1.1 as a representative usurpation threat node for Process->ExternalEntity flows.

title: Excessive Data Sharing with Parent
description: The portal may share more data with the parent than necessary for the intended purpose. For example, detailed submission history or internal feedback notes might be disclosed beyond what's needed for parental oversight.
assumptions: The data minimization principle is not fully applied when determining what data to share with parents.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 as a representative data minimization threat node.

title: Administrator Identifies Students via Account Data
description: School Administrator (EE4) creates and modifies accounts containing names, emails, and parent-child relationships, enabling direct identification of students and parents through the Grades Portal Web App (P1).
assumptions: Administrator has access to view and modify all account data including personal identifiers.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student/Parent Information
description: Administrator (EE4) can create, modify, and disable accounts with names, emails, roles, and relationships. If access controls are insufficient, this data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties or misused.
assumptions: Administrator has broad access to account data without adequate audit controls.

title: Linkability of Student/Parent Data Across Systems
description: Administrator (EE4) creates accounts linking names, emails, and parent-child relationships. This enables linking of data across different systems or contexts, potentially revealing connections between students and parents that could be exploited.
assumptions: Account data is stored in a way that allows cross-referencing and linking.

title: Administrator Usurpation of Student/Parent Identity
description: Administrator (EE4) has the ability to create and modify accounts, potentially enabling impersonation or usurpation of student or parent identities within the Grades Portal Web App (P1).
assumptions: Administrator has sufficient privileges to create accounts with any role or relationship.

title: Linkability of student-family relationships across systems
description: The grading service writes account records containing parent-child relationship links to the account directory. These relationships could be linked with other data sources (e.g., enrollment records, financial aid data) to create comprehensive profiles of students and their families, potentially revealing sensitive family connections.
assumptions: Other systems exist that contain complementary data about students or families
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a reasonable node for linkability threats in Process→DataStore flows

title: Identification of students and family members through account records
description: Account records written by the grading service contain parent-child relationship links that could be used to identify specific students and their family members. This identification could occur through direct access to the account directory or through correlation with other data sources.
assumptions: Account records contain sufficient identifying information (names, IDs, relationships)
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 as a reasonable node for identification threats in Process→DataStore flows

title: Unauthorized disclosure of account records to external parties
description: The account directory stores sensitive account records and parent-child relationship links written by the grading service. Without proper access controls, these records could be disclosed to unauthorized internal or external parties, potentially exposing student and family information.
assumptions: The account directory has access controls that may be insufficient or bypassed
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as a reasonable node for disclosure threats in Process→DataStore flows

title: Tampering with account records and relationship links
description: The grading service writes account records and parent-child relationship links to the account directory. These records could be modified by unauthorized actors or even by the grading service itself without proper audit trails, leading to incorrect or fraudulent data.
assumptions: The account directory lacks adequate integrity controls and audit logging
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 as a reasonable node for data modification threats in Process→DataStore flows

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third-Party Cloud Provider
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transferred to external cloud hosting provider EE5. This represents explicit disclosure of personal data across organizational boundary to a third party.
assumptions: The cloud provider has access to all personal data including grades and account information.

title: Linkability of Personal Data Across Systems
description: Grade records and account directory data transferred to cloud provider could be linked to identify specific individuals, potentially enabling cross-referencing with other data sources.
assumptions: Cloud provider may have access to additional data that could be correlated with the transferred data.

title: Identifiability of Students Through Account Directory
description: Account directory data contains personally identifiable information that could identify students/users, creating privacy risks when stored on external cloud infrastructure.
assumptions: Account directory includes names, IDs, or other identifiers that can be used to identify individuals.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Grade Records
description: Grade records from the database could be exposed to unauthorized parties during the read operation by the grading service, potentially revealing sensitive academic information about students, parents, and teachers.
assumptions: The grading service has vulnerabilities or insufficient access controls on the database connection.

title: Identification of Students and Parents via Grade Records
description: Grade records contain personally identifiable information that could be used to identify specific students, parents, and teachers, potentially leading to privacy violations when accessed by unauthorized entities.
assumptions: Grade records include student IDs, names, and contact information.

title: Excessive Data Collection for Multiple Views
description: The grading service may collect and process more grade record data than necessary to build student, parent, and teacher views, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: The service retrieves all grade records rather than filtering to only necessary data for each view.

title: Usurpation of Student or Parent Identity
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate a student or parent to access grade records through the grading service, especially if authentication mechanisms are weak.
assumptions: The grading service has inadequate authentication or authorization controls.

title: Linkability of Grade Records Across Views
description: Grade records could be linked across different views (student, parent, teacher) to create a comprehensive profile of individuals, potentially revealing more information than intended.
assumptions: The grading service maintains separate views that could be correlated by an attacker.
